heading: RNOR Status: Saving Tax on Foreign Income for Returning NRIs
tldr: Returning Non-Resident Indians (NRIs) can qualify for Resident Not Ordinarily Resident (RNOR) status for a few years.
RNOR status offers a significant tax advantage, as most foreign-sourced income is not taxable in India.
This includes income like foreign rental income, interest from overseas bank accounts, and capital gains from foreign assets.
To qualify, specific conditions related to your physical presence in India over recent years must be met.
Strategic financial planning during the RNOR period is crucial to optimise your tax position upon return.
caption:
Coming back to India after living abroad? Here's good news for your finances! You might qualify for a special tax status called RNOR for a few years. This means you won't pay Indian tax on most of your foreign income, like rent from your overseas property or interest from foreign bank accounts. It's a big saving! Learn how this can benefit you and what to plan for in our full article.
